title: The Regal session Rene Hall arranged in New Jersey, with Cooper and Chambers
summary: Fields pays for a bootleg union session in Jersey; the record featuring Cooper on baritone later turns up as a hit in Europe.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I think so too. I'll tell you a youngster (inaudible) while Leroy was in the band, a man who was about perhaps forty five, we were in New York, and I was still struggling to get another record session but it just looked like I couldn't get it, it was always something. When I talked to somebody I didn't like the way they wanted
me to record and I'd pass it up and go on and it was pretty hard; I had to hustle around with personal appearances to keep the name up.

Well anyway, Rene Hall was in New York City doing pretty well and had nice connections and I played the Apollo Theatre and was working in that area and I told Rene if there was some kind of way that I could get a session; he said I don't know, the syndicate is funny, unless some of them got a piece of your band or this and that and so on, and so finally he said, I'll tell you what, if you can pay for a session yourself, I have a friend that owns a studio, I know we're all union and everything, but we may bootleg a deal over there to pay for me, pay and record. So anyway, I said if we're going to do that, find me a couple of good men to go along.
So anyway, we went into New York and we met him in Jersey, the Regal Company, and we did an original, a couple of us got together and the band jammed around and we did a

number, an instrumental number featuring Cooper on baritone sax, and it went so well and everything, they were just tickled, we released it and Chambers--did you ever know Chambers the trombone player?
Well Chambers was on this session.

So anyway, I never did see that record anywhere in the states, but I got hold a few, and years later, when Cooper was with Ray Charles and he happened to come to Tulsa and he was laughing about an incident when he was in Europe. He said some musician came backstage and had a magazine and went to looking around and asking everybody's name and getting autographs like they do from the musicians, and so they spoke to Chambers before they did him and they said, you used to be with Ernie Fields and Chambers said no, I know Ernie Fields, but
I never was in his band, I just know him indirectly. Maybe I met him, I don't know. And so he said why did you ask me that? He said I have one of the records that you're on.

Yeah, and he said it's a big hit here. Then he looked over and he said, who is Leroy Cooper and Leroy said yeah, I was with Ernie Fields several years and then he thought, he said, you know what it is Chambers, that session, you did that session.
Now are we talking about Henderson Chambers or Dewey Chambers? There were two.
Were both of them trombone men?
I'm not sure; it loses me at this moment.
I forget the first name, but it was Chambers on trombone.
So they had the recording in Europe and released it?
